lines: Lost two arrows, kept my nerve. I will call that a fair trade.
My quiver is lighter, but I am home.
I counted arrows until counting steps mattered more.
My hands remembered what to do before my head caught up.
I made it back with an empty quiver and new respect for walls.
The road home looked farther after the fighting.
A steady breath is harder when the dark is shouting.
I lost my aim for a moment, not the way home.
I am still listening for footsteps behind me.
The first hit frightened me more than I want to admit.
I kept moving because standing still felt worse.
Someone covered me when I could not protect myself.
I lost track of time once the arrows started flying.
My hands began shaking only after we were safe.
I used every useful thing I had packed.
One dry string made the difference.
I know which piece of gear I will replace first.
We survived because people warned one another.
I will not laugh at practice drills again.
The noise made distance impossible to judge.
